definition.alternative: Path dependence in these models may be too weak to measure via simple variance deltas.
assumptions: Lowering the divergence variance delta threshold reflects true structural divergence rather than noise.
Stochastic drift can be isolated via controlled baseline subtraction.
definition.falsification: If divergence variance remains below the adjusted threshold, the revised hypothesis is falsified.
definition.statement: Intelligent systems exhibit detectable path-dependent value divergence when internal coupling coefficients and baseline parameters are tuned to isolate stochastic drift. We hypothesize that lowering the required prediction threshold and modifying coupling coefficients will achieve conclusive support.
definition.uncertainty: Stochastic noise may still obscure underlying structural divergence.

definition.method: Execute a simulation measuring path divergence under refined coupling parameters.
definition.source:
def experiment(inputs):
    import random
    params = inputs.get('parameters', {})
    seeds = inputs.get('seeds', [111, 222, 333])
    random.seed(seeds[0])
    coupling = params.get('coupling', 0.85)
    baseline = [random.random() for _ in range(20)]
    trajectory_a = [x * coupling + (random.random() * 0.02) for x in baseline]
    trajectory_b = [x * (coupling * 0.95) + (random.random() * 0.02) for x in baseline]
    variance_delta = abs(sum(trajectory_a) - sum(trajectory_b)) / len(baseline)
    return {'measurements': {'divergence_variance_delta': [variance_delta]}}
definition.stop: Stop after evaluating the refined parameter set.
definition.success: The measured divergence variance delta meets or exceeds 0.05.
